Target_Term_Definition: An Among-among is Tengger's protection rite for 44-day-old babies. The term derives from the word among (“to care for, to nurture”), and in reduplicated form refers to a special slametan or feast to show gratitude for children. The ritual includes the recitation of protective mantras at each stage of the baby’s development, along with prohibitions imposed on the mother, such as avoidance of consuming sea fish, spicy food, and cucumbers and recommendation of consuming ranti,sawijo, and tetirem leaves. After 44 days, the prohibitions are lifted and household life returns to normal.
Rationale: Sangat relevan (target utama) karena secara spesifik mendefinisikan ritus selamatan perlindungan bagi bayi berusia 44 hari di kalangan masyarakat Tengger.

Target_Term_Definition: A traditional haircut ritual performed to mark a child’s transition from infancy to childhood. The ceremony involves trimming the tip of the child's hair (kuncung) accompanied by prayers and offerings as a plea for safety and healthy growth.
Rationale: Memiliki relevansi karena merupakan ritus pemotongan ujung rambut (kuncung) untuk menandai peralihan anak dari masa bayi menuju kanak-kanak.

Target_Term_Definition: A traditional pregnancy ritual performed in Tengger before childbirth to pray for safety and a smooth delivery. In this ritual, a traditional midwife (dukun alit) prepares offerings on a woven tray (tampah), which are presented by her husband to Sang Hyang Widhi Wasa, with variations across different villages.
Rationale: Terkait erat dalam rangkaian siklus kelahiran di Tengger karena merupakan upacara selamatan kehamilan menjelang kelahiran bayi.

Target_Term_Definition: The Panji cycle: an East Javanese body of stories about a prince and princess separated, disguised, and reunited, which supplies the plots of the masked theatre.
Rationale: Sangat relevan (target utama) karena mendefinisikan siklus kisah Jawa Timur tentang pangeran dan putri kerajaan yang terpisah, menyamar, dan bersatu kembali sebagai sumber lakon teater topeng.

Target_Term_Definition: The masked dance-drama of Malang: episodes of the Panji cycle performed by dancers in carved wooden masks, accompanied by gamelan and narrated by a dhalang.
Rationale: Target utama yang sepadan karena merupakan dramatari topeng khas Malang yang mementaskan kisah bangsawan kerajaan dari siklus Panji.

Target_Term_Definition: The hero of the cycle, prince of Jenggala. Danced in the refined style, in a white mask with narrow eyes and a level gaze.
Rationale: Terkait erat karena merupakan tokoh pahlawan utama bergelar Pangeran Jenggala dalam lakon dramatari siklus Panji.

Target_Term_Definition: The heroine of the cycle, princess of Kediri, whose separation from and reunion with Panji drives the story.
Rationale: Memiliki relevansi karena merupakan tokoh utama putri Kerajaan Kediri yang menjadi pusat alur kisah dalam dramatari siklus Panji.

Target_Term_Definition: A pit or designated area used to collect and process organic materials, such as animal manure, for use as compost in traditional Javanese agricultural practices.
Rationale: Sangat relevan (target utama) karena secara spesifik mendefinisikan lubang atau tempat khusus untuk mengumpulkan dan mengolah kotoran ternak menjadi pupuk kompos dalam pertanian tradisional Jawa.

Target_Term_Definition: A traditional pregnancy ritual performed in Tengger before childbirth to pray for safety and a smooth delivery. In this ritual, a traditional midwife (dukun alit) prepares offerings on a woven tray (tampah), which are presented by her husband to Sang Hyang Widhi Wasa, with variations across different villages.
Rationale: Sangat relevan (target utama) karena secara eksplisit mendefinisikan ritual kehamilan tradisional di Tengger yang dilaksanakan menjelang persalinan untuk mendoakan keselamatan dan kelancaran melahirkan.

Target_Term_Definition: An Among-among is Tengger's protection rite for 44-day-old babies. The term derives from the word among (“to care for, to nurture”), and in reduplicated form refers to a special slametan or feast to show gratitude for children. The ritual includes the recitation of protective mantras at each stage of the baby’s development, along with prohibitions imposed on the mother, such as avoidance of consuming sea fish, spicy food, and cucumbers and recommendation of consuming ranti,sawijo, and tetirem leaves. After 44 days, the prohibitions are lifted and household life returns to normal.
Rationale: Terkait erat karena merupakan ritus perlindungan lanjutan pascapersalinan yang digelar saat bayi mencapai usia 44 hari.

Target_Term_Definition: A round flat tray made of woven bamboo strips, used for winnowing rice, drying food, and arranging ritual offerings in Javanese and Tengger traditions. Its circular form symbolizes wholeness and the interconnectedness of humans, nature, and the universe, representing receptivity to blessings in customary ceremonies.
Rationale: Memiliki relevansi karena merupakan nampan anyaman bambu bundar yang digunakan dukun alit untuk menata sesaji dalam upacara kehamilan Sayut.

Target_Term_Definition: A traditional Ponorogo figure with spiritual power. Warok refers to a figure in Ponorogo tradition believed to possess spiritual power or supernatural abilities. A Warok is often associated with strength, wisdom, moral authority, and the responsibility to protect and guide the community.
Rationale: Sangat relevan (target utama) karena mendefinisikan tokoh tradisional Ponorogo dalam kesenian Reog yang diyakini memiliki kesaktian spiritual, kekuatan, dan wibawa moral.

Target_Term_Definition: A powerful king of the Bantarangin Kingdom. Klono Sewandono is the king of the Bantarangin Kingdom in the Reog tradition, portrayed as a handsome, brave, and powerful ruler. In his dance performance, he wields the Samandiman whip, which has five strands (jabung sayet), symbolizing the strength of faith. This represents the belief that a true leader must possess firm faith grounded in the five pillars of Islam: the shahada, prayer, fasting, zakat, and hajj.
Rationale: Target utama yang sepadan karena didefinisikan sebagai raja penguasa Kerajaan Bantarangin yang gagah berani dan penuh kekuatan (powerful king) dalam tradisi Reog.

Target_Term_Definition: Warok Sepuh is a respected senior warok who carries a staff (teken) and serves as a mentor, teaching martial arts and the virtues of life to young waroks as part of the process of passing down noble values to the next generation.
Rationale: Terkait erat karena merupakan tokoh warok senior yang disegani dan menjadi mentor pewaris ilmu bela diri serta nilai luhur kepada warok muda.

Target_Term_Definition: A young male dancer in performances. Gemblak refers to a young male dancer who traditionally accompanied a warok in Reog Ponorogo performances, taking the role of the jathil, a horse-riding warrior, and wearing feminine-style attire such as a skirt, chest covering, and earrings as part of the symbolic presentation. The relationship between warok and gemblak was understood as a father–child spiritual bond, in which the warok practiced strict ascetic discipline, including abstaining from sexual relations, and the gemblak assisted the warok in daily needs as an expression of devotion rather than sexual orientation. Starting in the 1980s, the role of gemblak as jathil dancer was gradually replaced by women, marking a significant change in the Reog Ponorogo tradition.
Rationale: Memiliki relevansi karena merupakan penari muda yang memiliki ikatan pengabdian spiritual langsung untuk mendampingi kehidupan sehari-hari seorang warok.

Target_Term_Definition: A ritual container used for holding tirta or holy water in Tengger customary ceremonies. Used in rituals such as walagara, weddings, and funerary rites, it serves as a medium of purification and a conduit of blessings. The water within it, known as air wasuh padha, is used to wash the feet of ancestors or deities, symbolically purifying humans and bridging the spiritual and physical realms.
Rationale: Target utama leksikon yang merujuk langsung pada wadah ritual penyimpan tirta atau air suci dalam upacara adat masyarakat Tengger.

Target_Term_Definition: A sacred ceremonial space in the middle of the sand field at Mount Bromo, serving as the main altar during the Kasada ceremony in the Tengger community. At this site, shamans lead prayers and worship directed toward spiritual protectors such as Sunan Pernata, using ritual implements such as prapen (incense holder), prasen (holy water vessel), and offerings. It functions as the center of veneration, spiritual unity, and sacred communication between humans and the divine realm in Tengger religious tradition.
Rationale: Terkait erat karena merupakan altar suci di Gunung Bromo tempat para dukun adat memimpin doa menggunakan wadah air suci prasen dan pedupaan prapen.

Target_Term_Definition: An ancient kingdom in folklore. Bantarangin refers to the Bantarangin Kingdom, which appears in the folklore associated with Reog Ponorogo. The kingdom was ruled by Prabu Klanasewandana and his prime minister, Bujangganong, who sought to propose to the princess of Kediri, Dewi Songgolangit, under conditions that ultimately led to the creation of the Reog performance tradition. Bantarangin is often portrayed as a prosperous and powerful kingdom, and its story serves as a narrative foundation for explaining the origins of Reog Ponorogo.
Rationale: Target utama leksikon yang merujuk langsung pada kerajaan kuno dalam cerita rakyat yang menjadi landasan kisah asal-usul Reog Ponorogo.

Target_Term_Definition: An early form of Reog from Bantarangin. Reog Bantarangin is considered the earliest form of Reog, originating from the Bantarangin Kingdom (the western river bank version). It features a complex dance-drama structure with characters such as the Warok that is the horse-riding Jathil warriors, Patih Bujangganing, Prabu Klomosewandana, and Dadak Merak. This version presents the storyline with clearly defined roles for each character and follows a strict, standardized performance structure.
Rationale: Target utama yang sepadan karena merujuk langsung pada bentuk awal kesenian Reog yang berasal dari Kerajaan Bantarangin.

Target_Term_Definition: A powerful king of the Bantarangin Kingdom. Klono Sewandono is the king of the Bantarangin Kingdom in the Reog tradition, portrayed as a handsome, brave, and powerful ruler. In his dance performance, he wields the Samandiman whip, which has five strands (jabung sayet), symbolizing the strength of faith. This represents the belief that a true leader must possess firm faith grounded in the five pillars of Islam: the shahada, prayer, fasting, zakat, and hajj.
Rationale: Terkait erat karena merupakan tokoh raja penguasa Kerajaan Bantarangin yang gagah berani dalam tradisi Reog Ponorogo.

Target_Term_Definition: A warlord figure from the Bantarangin Kingdom. Pujangga Anom, also known as Pujangganong or Bujanganom, is a warlord figure from the Bantarangin Kingdom who embodies an energetic, agile, and acrobatic military leader, reflecting the noble qualities of a patih who is devoted and responsible in managing the kingdom's strategic affairs. His lively and acrobatic dance movements make this character especially appealing to audiences, accompanied by the use of a mask with bulging eyes as a symbol of sharpness, alertness, and precision in carrying out the commands of King Prabu Klono Sewandono. Physically, the dancer typically wears a white half-face mask with a blunt nose, identified as the Pëntoel mask, although according to Mr. Staugaard, there are also dancers who use black masks referred to by the same name, indicating variations in how this figure is represented in Reog performances.
Rationale: Memiliki relevansi karena merupakan tokoh patih dan panglima perang dari Kerajaan Bantarangin yang setia menjalankan perintah Prabu Klono Sewandono.

Target_Term_Definition: A traditional Ponorogo figure with spiritual power. Warok refers to a figure in Ponorogo tradition believed to possess spiritual power or supernatural abilities. A Warok is often associated with strength, wisdom, moral authority, and the responsibility to protect and guide the community.
Rationale: Target utama leksikon yang merujuk langsung pada tokoh masyarakat Ponorogo yang diyakini memiliki kekuatan spiritual, wibawa moral, dan peran pelindung warga.

Target_Term_Definition: Warok Sepuh is a respected senior warok who carries a staff (teken) and serves as a mentor, teaching martial arts and the virtues of life to young waroks as part of the process of passing down noble values to the next generation.
Rationale: Target utama yang sepadan karena merujuk langsung pada sosok warok senior pembawa tongkat (teken) yang menjadi mentor bagi para warok muda.

Target_Term_Definition: Kolor refers to loose black pants that are part of the warok costume. The material used is typically strong and comfortable, such as Nagata Drill fabric. These pants are worn by the warok to create a majestic and powerful appearance during performances.
Rationale: Terkait erat karena merupakan celana hitam longgar berbahan kuat yang menjadi bagian utama dari busana seorang warok.

Target_Term_Definition: A cantrik is a student or disciple who studies under the guidance of a spiritual figure or the leader of a spiritual retreat (such as a warok in the Reog tradition), faithfully following him wherever he goes to gain knowledge and learn the rituals and traditions of that way of life.
Rationale: Memiliki relevansi karena merupakan murid yang belajar dan mengabdi di bawah bimbingan tokoh spiritual seperti warok.

Target_Term_Definition: A traditional house developed and passed down through generations by the Samin community in Bojonegoro, characterized by a structural system of timber columns and beams that differs from the four main posts of a typical joglo. Its main structure consists of a foundation, soko guru, blandar, dudur, sunduk, pemeret, tuwuh, and uwun, which form the lower, middle, and roof structures of the house and are generally connected through simple purusan joints.
Rationale: Target utama leksikon yang merujuk langsung pada rumah tradisional warisan masyarakat Samin di Bojonegoro dengan sistem tiang dan balok kayu khas.

Target_Term_Definition: A structural post or pillar that supports the main framework of a traditional Javanese house, including the saka guru and pracik in a srotong house, each consisting of eight posts arranged in specific positions to support the roof and maintain the stability of the building.
Rationale: Terkait erat karena merupakan tiang penyangga utama kerangka bangunan yang mencakup delapan tiang saka guru dan pracik pada rumah srotong.

Target_Term_Definition: A supporting post or brace attached to a traditional house, particularly to reinforce and stabilize its walls. In a srotong house, dhanyang serves as an additional structural support and consists of eight posts.
Rationale: Memiliki relevansi karena merupakan delapan tiang penyangga tambahan yang berfungsi memperkuat dan menstabilkan dinding pada rumah srotong.

Target_Term_Definition: A wooden structural beam in a traditional Javanese building that connects and reinforces the main pillars of the structure. In Javanese house construction, sunduk is positioned beneath the blandar and pangeret  and is associated with the saka guru, the four main pillars supporting the building. This element forms part of the structural framework that binds the main pillars together and strengthens the building.
Rationale: Target utama leksikon yang merujuk langsung pada balok kayu pengikat dan penguat tiang-tiang utama (saka guru) pada bangunan tradisional Jawa.

Target_Term_Definition: A traditional house developed and passed down through generations by the Samin community in Bojonegoro, characterized by a structural system of timber columns and beams that differs from the four main posts of a typical joglo. Its main structure consists of a foundation, soko guru, blandar, dudur, sunduk, pemeret, tuwuh, and uwun, which form the lower, middle, and roof structures of the house and are generally connected through simple purusan joints.
Rationale: Terkait erat karena sunduk merupakan salah satu komponen balok struktural utama yang menyusun kerangka Rumah Srotong di Bojonegoro.
